title: Inexpensive Duvet with Minor Quality Issues
text:
Inexpensive Duvet with Minor Quality Issues. This duvet came pretty quickly after ordering. It's dyed a nice consistent color and is very soft (although microfiber, so if you sweat a lot, use a cotton top sheet under this). It came in simple, disposable, shrink-wrap packaging (unlike bedding which comes in a thick, plastic, zippered pouch so you can wash and store linens without them getting dusty, though, and typically purchase bedding that comes in this manner for this reason). The duvet cover is very thin, and appeared wrinkle-free, with clear buttons at one end and ties at each corner (on the inside), so you can tie the duvet to it.

As soon I'd opened it up, I'd decided to put it on the new, white down comforter that I had also purchased here on Amazon. After turning the duvet cover inside out and all four corners were tied to the comforter, I turned it all inside out (if you haven't learned to roll up a duvet and cover to put it on easier, check out a video on YouTube) and buttoned it up.

It looks pretty, but I had to sew part of the duvet cover, as the factory managed to miss a six inch portion at the top of the duvet cover that wasn't sewn. I was annoyed that right out of the gate there was an issue with quality, but I knew it wouldn't be an heirloom piece with the low thread count and the price I'd paid. The comforter was not that expensive, and I didn't have a lot of money to spend on a cover, but I just wanted to save the duvet from getting soiled with regular use. I think it will do the job but I suggest anyone buying this brand to do a quick quality check when your item comes in, so you can return it within the window. I'd not contacted the manufacturer because I don't have the time or energy to send it back, so I docked stars for a lack of quality control, instead.
